# cache-strategies

> Versão em português: [README.pt-BR.md](README.pt-BR.md)

A cache is a second copy of the data, and the whole difficulty is keeping the two copies together. This mini-project puts Redis in front of PostgreSQL behind an ElysiaJS API and shows two things. First, how the three classic strategies behave on a write (cache-aside, write-through and write-behind), each with a test that states what it guarantees and what it does not. Second, the cache stampede: 300 readers of one popular key send hundreds of identical queries to the database every time the key expires, and a lock or an early refresh brings that down to one.

Code: MP-CACHE-1. Full explanation: [docs/en/cache/cache-strategies.md](../../../docs/en/cache/cache-strategies.md).

## Results

Measured with k6 against the local API. Generated by the load test. Do not edit by hand.

### Stampede: database queries per expiry

300 virtual users read one hot key. The cached copy lives 2 s and the query behind it takes 100 ms.

<!-- stampede:start -->
| Protection | Rounds | Expiries | Database queries | Queries per expiry (median) | Queries per expiry (range) | p95 latency, ms (mean ± sd) | Slowest request (ms) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `none` | 3 | 9 | 2627 | **299** | 260 to 300 | 64 ± 51 | 1729 |
| `lock` | 3 | 15 | 15 | **1** | 1 | 107 ± 32 | 365 |
| `early` | 3 | 18 | 18 | **1** | 1 | 39 ± 23 | 289 |
<!-- stampede:end -->

Without protection every expiry is paid by the whole herd. With `lock` or `early` it is paid once. `early` also keeps the latency flat, because nobody waits for the reload.

### Hit rate and latency per strategy and time to live

20 virtual users, 200 products, 2% writes. Each database read costs an extra 5 ms.

<!-- hit-rate:start -->
| Strategy | Time to live | Rounds | Hit rate (mean ± sd) | Read median (ms) | Read p95, ms (mean ± sd) | Write median (ms) | Write p95 (ms) | DB reads per 1000 requests | DB writes per 1000 requests |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cache-aside` | 250 ms | 3 | 59.2% ± 4.2 | 3.34 | 17.3 ± 10.7 | 23.12 | 493.4 | 403.2 | 20.3 |
| `cache-aside` | 1000 ms | 3 | 85.1% ± 1.7 | 1.40 | 9.9 ± 4.7 | 13.80 | 50.0 | 147.5 | 21.5 |
| `cache-aside` | 5000 ms | 3 | 95.2% ± 0.6 | 1.29 | 8.0 ± 7.0 | 43.64 | 442.2 | 47.7 | 19.7 |
| `write-through` | 250 ms | 3 | 62.9% ± 5.9 | 3.06 | 16.7 ± 16.6 | 19.19 | 60.4 | 360.7 | 21.4 |
| `write-through` | 1000 ms | 3 | 83.8% ± 3.2 | 3.46 | 20.9 ± 10.0 | 20.92 | 77.2 | 157.3 | 20.1 |
| `write-through` | 5000 ms | 3 | 96.7% ± 1.3 | 2.31 | 15.0 ± 9.2 | 48.52 | 236.9 | 30.1 | 21.5 |
| `write-behind` | 250 ms | 3 | 55.2% ± 2.3 | 8.02 | 36.6 ± 10.9 | 11.14 | 39.9 | 455.3 | 5.5 |
| `write-behind` | 1000 ms | 3 | 83.2% ± 3.8 | 3.25 | 27.5 ± 15.2 | 7.04 | 33.2 | 164.0 | 4.5 |
| `write-behind` | 5000 ms | 3 | 97.4% ± 0.8 | 1.71 | 9.8 ± 8.2 | 2.43 | 13.6 | 25.4 | 3.2 |
<!-- hit-rate:end -->

Machine, versions and the definition of each column are in [results/results.md](results/results.md). The runs are short and the machine was shared, so the latencies are noisy. The query counts of the stampede table are the stable part.

## Quiz topics it demonstrates

- `cache` / `caching-strategies`: who writes where and in which order in cache-aside, write-through and write-behind, and what a write costs in each
- `cache` / `consistency-trade-offs`: the read that repopulates the cache with an old value, the database that is behind the cache in write-behind, the acknowledged write that is lost
- `cache` / `stampede-penetration-avalanche`: the stampede, the lock (`SET key token NX PX`) and the early refresh
- `cache` / `invalidation-ttl`: the time to live as the bound on staleness, and its effect on the hit rate

## Run

The only requirement is Docker.

```sh
./setup-unix-cache-strategies.sh        # Linux and macOS
./setup-windows-cache-strategies.ps1    # Windows
```

The script builds the image, runs the tests against a Redis and a PostgreSQL container on an internal network, and removes the containers at the end.

## Load test (the demo)

```sh
./load-test-unix.sh            # Linux and macOS
./load-test-windows.ps1        # Windows
```

One command, about 6 minutes: it starts the API, runs the stampede experiment for `none`, `lock` and `early`, runs the hit rate experiment for 3 strategies and 3 times to live, three rounds each, and rewrites `results/` and the two tables above. It fails when the unprotected run does not show at least 100 queries per expiry, or when a fix lets more than 1 through. Pass a number of rounds to change the default (`./load-test-unix.sh 1`, `.\load-test-windows.ps1 -Rounds 1`).

k6 only ever targets the `api` service of this compose file: the network is internal, no port is published, and both scripts refuse a `BASE_URL` that is not local (`k6/guard.js`).

## Tests

```sh
docker compose run --rm ts-test
docker compose down -v
```

The container runs the TypeScript type check and then `bun test`, against the real Redis and PostgreSQL.

| Strategy | Guarantee proved by a test | Limit proved by a test |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cache-aside` | After a write returns, the cached copy is gone and the next read is fresh | A read racing a write can cache the old value, and only the time to live removes it |
| `write-through` | When a write returns, database and cache both hold the new value, and the next read is a hit with no query. A write the database rejects never reaches the cache | The cached copy still needs a time to live |
| `write-behind` | Readers of the cache see the write at once. Many writes to one product inside an interval become one database write | The database is behind until the flush, and an acknowledged write is lost when the cache dies before it |

The stampede tests fire 200 simultaneous reads in-process and assert the same counts as the load test: 200 queries without protection, 1 with the lock, 1 with the early refresh.

## API

| Route | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /products/:strategy/:id` | Reads a product. `strategy` is `cache-aside`, `write-through` or `write-behind`. The `X-Cache` header says `hit` or `miss` |
| `PUT /products/:strategy/:id` | Body `{ "price": 1234 }` (cents). Writes with the chosen strategy |
| `GET /hot/:mode` | Reads the hot key of the stampede experiment. `mode` is `none`, `lock` or `early` |
| `POST /admin/reset` | Empties Redis, recreates the products and applies the settings of the next experiment (`products`, `ttlMs`, `queryCostMs`, `slowQueryMs`, `earlyRefreshMs`) |
| `POST /admin/flush` | Runs the write-behind flush now |
| `POST /admin/counters/reset` | Zeroes the counters, to leave a warm-up out of a measurement |
| `GET /stats` | Hits, misses, database reads and writes, and the queries of each expiry of the hot key |

## Structure

| Path | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `ts/src/strategies.ts` | The shared read path and the three write strategies, with the write-behind flush |
| `ts/src/stampede.ts` | The hot key: no protection, lock, early refresh, and the count of queries per expiry |
| `ts/src/cache.ts` | The Redis commands used, including the lock and its release script |
| `ts/src/db.ts` | The `products` table and the counted queries |
| `ts/src/app.ts` | The ElysiaJS routes, with Zod validation |
| `ts/src/report.ts` | Aggregates the k6 summaries and checks the acceptance criteria |
| `k6/stampede.js`, `k6/hit-rate.js` | The two load tests. `k6/guard.js` refuses non-local targets |
| `results/` | The committed results tables |

Nothing is imported from another mini-project. The layout of the compose file, the scripts and the report follows `projects/transactions/overselling-checkout`, copied and adapted.
